lines: Progressive weight gain, fatigue, and difficulty climbing stairs over 6 months

She reports her menstrual cycles have become irregular and she has developed new facial hair.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.
On examination, she has a rounded face, supraclavicular fat pads, and a dorsocervical fat hump.
Her skin appears thin with purple striae on the abdomen and easy bruising on her arms.

encounters.cc: Recurrent severe unilateral headaches for the past 6 months with visual disturbances

lines: Recurrent severe unilateral headaches for the past 6 months with visual disturbances
This 34-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and adrenal Cushing syndrome, recently diagnosed, presents to neurology for evaluation of headaches.
She describes the headaches as severe, unilateral, and throbbing, occurring about twice a month and lasting for several hours.
The headaches are often preceded by visual disturbances, including flashing lights and blind spots.
She also reports sensitivity to light and sound during these episodes, as well as nausea that occasionally leads to vomiting.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.
Her physical examination is unremarkable, and her blood pressure is well-controlled.

lines: Acute palpitations, weight loss despite increased appetite, and heat intolerance

- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.

encounters.cc: Routine ophthalmology examination for medication monitoring

lines: Routine ophthalmology examination for medication monitoring
The patient with SLE returns for medication monitoring with migraine aura history.
She reports no acute visual symptoms but mentions progressively worsened difficulty with night driving over the past year.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril, and a previous episode of lupus nephritis.
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
She has been on hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily for the past 4 years.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.
On examination, visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes.
Fundoscopy reveals bilateral pigmentary changes in the macula.
Automated visual field testing shows bilateral central scotomas.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of confusion and agitation 2 hours after cesarean section

lines: Sudden onset of confusion and agitation 2 hours after cesarean section

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, adrenal Cushing syndrome, and recent ophthalmologic monitoring for hydroxychloroquine retinopathy who presents following cesarean delivery.
She is brought to the emergency department by her husband due to sudden onset of confusion and agitation.
She had a cesarean section 2 hours ago under epidural anesthesia and was recovering well until she started complaining of a metallic taste in her mouth followed by perioral numbness.
Her husband also reports that she had a brief episode of jerking movements involving her whole body.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.
Blood pressure 145/95 mmHg, heart rate 102 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F)
She is disoriented to time and place.
Her pupils are dilated but reactive to light, and she has increased muscle tone with hyperreflexia.
There is no evidence of trauma.
- Complete blood count: within normal limits

encounters.cc: Worsening headaches, nausea, vomiting, and transient visual disturbances over 2 weeks

lines: Worsening headaches, nausea, vomiting, and transient visual disturbances over 2 weeks

This 37-year-old female with breast cancer in surveillance and prior migraine with aura presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of worsening headaches, primarily at night, and episodes of morning nausea and vomiting.
She also reports transient visual disturbances.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
Her medical history is significant for breast cancer, for which she completed chemotherapy 6 months ago.
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.
Her blood pressure is 165/95 mmHg, heart rate is 55 bpm, and respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute.
On examination, she is alert but appears anxious.
Neurological examination shows no focal deficits.
- Complete blood count (CBC): within normal limits
A CT scan of the head without contrast shows a 3 cm mass lesion in the right cerebral hemisphere with surrounding edema.

encounters.cc: Acute palpitations, chest tightness, and feeling of impending doom

lines: Acute palpitations, chest tightness, and feeling of impending doom
This 37-year-old with prior atrial fibrillation and recent brain metastasis presents acutely.
She reports that these symptoms began suddenly while shopping at a grocery store.
She has experienced similar episodes over the past 6 months, which have been increasing in frequency.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
Her past medical history is significant for generalized anxiety disorder.
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
She denies any use of caffeine, alcohol, or illicit drugs.
On examination, her heart rate is 110 bpm, blood pressure is 140/85 mmHg, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute.
She appears anxious and is trembling.
Her serum electrolytes, thyroid function tests, and complete blood count are within normal limits.
An electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia with no acute ST changes.

encounters.cc: Tingling around mouth and fingertips with acute anxiety

lines: Tingling around mouth and fingertips with acute anxiety

The patient is a 38-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, breast cancer on surveillance following prior treatment for brain metastases, and generalized anxiety disorder, who returns to the emergency department six months after a prior visit for similar symptoms.
She presents with complaints of tingling around her mouth and in her fingertips.
She has a history of anxiety and reports that she has been experiencing recurrent panic attacks over the past week.
During these episodes, she feels short of breath and has a sensation of impending doom, which prompts her to breathe rapidly and deeply for several minutes.
- Breast cancer (status post chemotherapy, surveillance phase)
- Left breast lumpectomy with sentinel lymph node biopsy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Coordinator.
Her respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute,
Her heart rate is 98 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg.
On examination, she is alert and oriented, but appears anxious.
and she is taking deep, regular breaths.
